consensus_summary: Sand primarily means an innumerable multitude (esp. Abraham’s descendants per covenant, also armies/peoples/abundance); common alternative is unstable/foolish foundation (Matt 7 parable); minority uses are divine boundary restraining the sea and image of weight/burden. Meanings are context-driven; popular teaching often elevates the foundation image.
book_summary: Countless multitude (grains of the shore beyond number) and therefore a shifting foundation: to build on the sand is to build on the crowd, not the covenant-rock.
consensus_core_identification: innumerable multitude (Abrahamic seed etc.); unstable foundation
book_core_identification: countless multitude that is a shifting foundation (crowd vs. covenant-rock)
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies the two main consensus senses by treating the foundation image as derivative of the multitude (‘and so’) and re-specifies parabolic sand as ‘the crowd’ opposed to ‘covenant-rock’; consensus keeps the senses independent and context-specific without that causal equation or crowd re-identification.
rationale: Minimum cores match: both center on sand-as-innumerable-multitude (Gen/Hos/Rev) plus sand-as-unstable-foundation (Matt 7). The book preserves these referents but materially alters boundary and precision by synthesizing them into one complex and reclassifying the parable’s sand as the human crowd rather than generic physical instability. This is refinement of extension/conditions, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: The causal link (‘and so’) and the specific equation of parabolic sand with ‘the crowd’ (vs. rock as ‘covenant-rock’) are interpretive additions not required by the cited texts, which present the images independently.
